title: Six operations on Weil complexes
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$, and fix a prime $\ell\neq p$; write
$\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and
let $E/\Ql$ be finite and contained in $\Qlb$, and let
$\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$; use the
Weil-complex category, the
bounded constructible
coefficient categories and their
finite-Tor subcategories, the
separated finite-type
morphism conditions, and the
exceptional-adjoint
admissibility condition in its constructible form (the exceptional inverse
image of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], defined for every separated
finite-type morphism; the ambient clause (1) of
[def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility] is not assumed, as it fails in
general). Use the
derived pullback, tensor, and
internal-Hom operations, the
derived direct-image and
compact-support direct image, the
exceptional inverse image, the
exchange/projection transformations, and
the standard truncation functors $\tau^{\leq m},\tau^{\geq m}$.
Let $X_0,Y_0$ be
finite-type $k_0$-schemes
and let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a
separated finite-type
$k_0$-morphism, and let
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be
the geometric fiber of
$f_0$. For
$K\in D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(X,\Lambda)$, and, whenever a tensor or internal
Hom is used on a scheme $W\in\{X,Y\}$, for
$M\in D^b_{ctf}(W,\Lambda)$ and $N\in D^b_c(W,\Lambda)$, the exact functors

$$
Lf^*,\quad Rf_*,\quad Rf_!,\quad -\otimes^L-,\quad R\mathcal Hom
$$

lift to Weil complexes on every one of these domains on which their
underlying bounded constructibility has been proved. In particular, the
elementary internal-Hom preservation theorem applies when its first
argument is site-perfect. Equivariance itself supplies no preservation
theorem for a larger domain. Put

$$
g_X=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q),
\qquad
g_Y=\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q),
$$

using the geometric-Frobenius convention.
The constructible exceptional inverse image $Rf^!$ of
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] — available for every separated
finite-type $f$, so that no admissibility hypothesis is needed — also has an
equivariant lift, with its Weil
isomorphism induced by the corresponding exchange and adjunction maps. For
example, the Weil isomorphism on $Rf_*K$ is

$$
Lg_Y^*Rf_*\operatorname{For}(K)
\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Ex}_*}
Rf_*Lg_X^*\operatorname{For}(K)
\xrightarrow{Rf_*(\theta_K)}Rf_*\operatorname{For}(K),
$$

and the compact-support construction uses $\operatorname{Ex}_!$.
For every $W\in\{X,Y\}$ and $m\in\mathbf Z$, let
$\tau^{\leq m},\tau^{\geq m}:D^b_c(W,\Lambda)\to D^b_c(W,\Lambda)$
be the truncation functors, characterized by vanishing of the
cohomology sheaves
$\mathcal H^r(\tau^{\leq m}K)=0$ for $r>m$ and
$\mathcal H^r(\tau^{\geq m}K)=0$ for $r<m$, together with their
standard truncation triangles. The
forgetful functor commutes with these lifted operations. Composition,
base change, projection, purity, and duality isomorphisms are morphisms of
Weil complexes and induce Frobenius-equivariant maps on
cohomology.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pod-semilinear-field-operation-lifts] to the geometric fibers and the stated preserved domains. Its semilinear transport equivalences and five explicit fixed-pair formulas give the lifts of $Lf^*,Rf_*,Rf_!$, tensor and internal Hom, functoriality on arrows, and the displayed $Rf_*$ formula. Their forgetful images are the given operations. Retain the finite-Tor/site-perfect restrictions of each underlying preservation theorem.

source.place: Proof sentence 1: semilinear Frobenius square, exact rational transport, and explicit operation/evaluation lifts; returned proof Steps 1–2.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pod-constructible-mate-coherence] with $S=P_X$, $T=P_Y$ and $a=\operatorname{Ex}_!$. The equivalences needed there are supplied by Step 1; the canonical exchange is invertible by [lem-pod-weil-frobenius-compact-support-exchange]. The lemma's mate gives the constructible $Rf^!$ lift and equivariant unit and counit, and identifies the pasted exceptional comparisons. It also gives equivariance of composition, exchange and projection transformations, and of their inverses wherever already proved invertible. No ambient adjoint or separatedness of the base is used.

source.place: Proof sentence 1: exceptional adjunction, its unit/counit, comparison maps and mate pasting; returned proof Steps 3–4 and 6.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pod-fixed-pair-truncation-cohomology] for $W=X,Y$. It gives both lifted truncations, all canonical truncation-triangle arrows and induced cohomology-sheaf structures. For maps pushed to the coefficient point, use the lifted direct images and equivariant comparisons from Steps 1–2; the same lemma's point-transport equation gives Frobenius-equivariant maps on ordinary and compactly supported cohomology groups whenever defined.

source.place: Proof sentence 2: truncation maps and all truncation-triangle arrows; final assertion on cohomology; returned proof Steps 5 and 11.

proof.text: On the smooth purity domains apply [lem-pod-rational-purity-pairing]. Its mate identification is exactly the exceptional lift of Step 2, so its rational naturality equation makes canonical purity and smooth trace equivariant. On the smooth site-perfect Poincare domain its evaluation–trace pairing has the inverse contravariant datum and scalar $q^{-d}$, giving the twisted pairing equation for arbitrary rational Weil isomorphisms.

source.place: Proof sentence 3 (orientation and trace) and sentence 4 final clause (smooth pairing), for arbitrary rational Weil isomorphisms; returned proof Steps 7 and 10.

proof.text: On each stated duality domain apply [lem-pod-formal-verdier-exchange-equivariance], using the operation lifts and equivariant adjunction/composition maps of Steps 1–2. It supplies rational duality, evaluation and biduality, coefficient-extension compatibility and equivariance of the specified formal Verdier exchange; invertibility retains the underlying theorem's hypotheses. Together with Steps 1–4 this covers every comparison in the statement. Forgetting recovers the original maps, and Step 3 gives their equivariance on cohomology.

source.place: Proof sentence 4: rational duality/evaluation and the explicit projection–evaluation–transpose construction of formal Verdier exchange; returned proof Steps 8–9.

proof_origin.place: Entire proof, expanded with the fixed-pair and mate calculations; all geometric inputs cited as existing DAG nodes
